Audit log

WhatEverFi keeps a record of who did what in each organization: which bot or person took an action, what was approved and by whom, and which settings and credentials changed. Recording is always on.

Organization owners and admins can export it as JSON Lines, and operators can forward it to a SIEM.

What is recorded

Action When
tool.call A bot ran a consequential tool, or was refused one by a rule (outcome is success, failure or denied)
approval.decided A person allowed or denied an action a bot asked for
approval.auto_reviewed The auto-reviewer judged an action (metadata.decision)
approval.policy.changed Approval mode, allow/block rules, or a space setting changed
credential.created, credential.changed, credential.deleted, credential.revealed Model, MCP, connector, voice, memory, vault and bot secrets
space.created, space.renamed, space.deleted Spaces
auth.sign_in, auth.sign_out, auth.password.changed, auth.passkey.*, auth.session.revoked, device.* Account security, recorded in each organization the account belongs to
auth.account.deactivated, auth.account.reactivated The identity provider (directory provisioning) or the operator turned an account off or back on; the actor is the system, labelled directory or operator
audit_log.exported Someone exported the audit log

Each event has the time, actor (user, bot or system, with a display label), action, target, outcome, space, run and chat ids, the client address and user agent for people, and a few identifiers. Labels are copied when the event is written, so the record still reads correctly after the space, chat, run, bot or account is deleted. Events never include message content, tool arguments, or secret values.

Actor labels (a person’s email), client addresses and user agents stay in the log after the account is deleted, until retention prunes them, and in any SIEM they were forwarded to.

Rows are never updated. Postgres rejects updates, and the only delete is retention pruning. Failed sign-ins, rate limits and refused destinations have no organization to belong to; they stay in the deployment’s security events.

Retention

AUDIT_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 365) sets how long events are kept. Pruning runs about once an hour on the elected reconciler, so one instance prunes however many run.

Forwarding to a SIEM

Set AUDIT_LOG_WEBHOOK_URL to an HTTPS endpoint and the reconciler posts every event to it, oldest first, as application/x-ndjson (one JSON event per line, the same shape as the export). AUDIT_LOG_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION, when set, is sent as the Authorization header, for example Bearer <token> or Splunk <token>.

Delivery is at least once: deduplicate on id. Events are sent about a minute after they are written. When the endpoint fails, WhatEverFi keeps its place and retries with backoff up to an hour apart, so nothing is skipped while it is down. Events pruned by retention before they are delivered are not sent.

Export and API

GET /api/audit-events/export returns the organization’s events as JSON Lines, newest first, for a signed-in owner or admin. It accepts from and to (ISO 8601), spaceId, actorId and action filters. The audit.events RPC returns the same events in pages with a nextCursor.
